label-mid.purpose: Proof links, the action links, the availability line.

jump.purpose: The jump list in the pinned column, uppercased and tracked.

label.purpose: The running head's nav, the credential, the skip link. The nav drops to 12.5px below 440px.

section-label.purpose: A section's own name, in diluted ink over a stronger hairline, set smaller than the body it introduces.

fonts.name: Source Serif 4 Italic

fonts.name: Geist Mono

motion.name: duration-jump
motion.purpose: The jump rule's scaleX and background colour on hover and on focus-visible.

motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion both transitions are removed outright, so hover states arrive at full value instantly and smooth scrolling is off.

breakpoints.name: single-column
breakpoints.purpose: The shell collapses to a block, the identity column becomes the opening block at 44rem with its jump list hidden, the stream and footer cap at 44rem, and the running head appears. scroll-padding-top goes to 74px.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Body drops to 17.5px, the gutter to 20px, every record grid becomes a block with its rail folded under the name as an inline wrapping row, kit rows collapse to one column, and the prose indents reset to 0.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: The wordmark leaves the running head and the four nav destinations spread across its full width at 12.5px.

breakpoints.name: short-viewport
breakpoints.purpose: The pinned identity column goes position: static, since it would otherwise be taller than the window and clip itself.

layout.shell: 75.5rem, grid of var(--ident) and minmax(0, 1fr), column-gap clamp(40px, 5vw, 78px), align-items start
layout.identColumn: clamp(15rem, 21vw, 19rem), position: sticky at top 0, padding clamp(38px, 4.2vw, 58px) 0 30px
layout.recordGrid: clamp(4.75rem, 6vw, 7rem) of rail against minmax(0, 1fr), column-gap 28px; heading first in source, rail placed at 1 / 1 / span 40 / span 1 with align-self start
layout.leftEdges: two: the rail's, shared by the date rails and the section labels, and the prose's, picked up outside a record grid with calc(var(--rail) + var(--rail-gap))
layout.runningHead: display: none above 980px; below it sticky and opaque in the page ground with a 1px soft hairline, never blurred

extensions.forcedColors: Under forced-colors: active the four CSS marks (the 5px bullet, the rail's live square, the availability square and the 44px jump rule) are painted CanvasText with forced-color-adjust: none, and the jump rule takes Highlight on hover and on focus-visible.
extensions.print: The print stylesheet redefines the tokens rather than overriding rules: ground #fff, ink #000, ink-2 #444, rule #999, rule-soft #c4c4c4, and both link and live #000. The running head, skip link, jump list and availability line are hidden; the shell and every record grid become blocks; body sets 11pt; sections take 20pt of lead with break-inside: avoid on sections, records, posts and short records; and the proof, contact, action and resume links print their href after the text at 8.5pt in #555.
constraints: One static index.html with all CSS in a single inline <style>, no framework and no build step.
One line of authored JavaScript (the footer year) plus a deferred analytics tag; no content may depend on a script.
No raster images anywhere. The favicon is an inline SVG data URI and it is the only graphic.
100 Lighthouse on all four categories on both the desktop and mobile presets, verified per change.
No backdrop-filter on the running head, no mask over an animated subtree, and no animated layer larger than the viewport plus one tile.

narrative.overview:
This is a working engineer's own site, set as a register that stays open at the identity page. A narrow column on the left holds the name, the role, one jump link per section, the resume, the three ways to reach him and the availability line, and it is pinned to the top of the viewport so it is on screen at every scroll position. The wide column on the right is a stream of records in dated rows. Every row opens with its year standing in a rail at the left edge, so a reader scanning for when can run a finger down one column while the prose keeps a second left edge of its own from the top of the page to the bottom.

The material is a cold neutral grey-black ground under a near-white ink, and the page carries a light mode on the system setting where the ground warms slightly and the ink inverts. Both inks in each scheme are mixed from the same cold hue, so the secondary ink sits inside the primary's family as a second real ink. One amber is the only hue in the file, and it does exactly two jobs: it carries every link and it marks what is live. Nothing is boxed. Structure is carried by two weights of 1px hairline, the rail's own left edge, and space, so the page has no containers to decorate and no surfaces to tint.

Two faces divide the page by role. Source Serif 4, a text serif with a true italic, sets every sentence a person wrote. Geist Mono sets the fields a reader scans down a column instead of reading: status, years and dates, stack names, proof links, and the section labels themselves. The type scale is inverted at the section label: a label is 12.5px tracked mono standing over 17px and 18px prose, so the record names and the sentences are the only things on the page carrying weight. The craft bar is set by three named reference sites, simonwillison.net, overreacted.io and danluu.com. The page refuses the generated-portfolio vocabulary outright, because that vocabulary is the thing this site was rebuilt four times to escape: equal-weight rounded cards with soft shadows, gradients, glass, saturated pill badges, emoji icons and an indigo-to-violet accent are all out, and so is any costume or theme, since the look is earned from type, measure and real data.
keyCharacteristics: Two columns inside a 75.5rem shell: a pinned identity column and a stream of records
Every record is a grid whose first column is a date rail, with the heading first in source order
Dark is the base scheme and light is the media-query override
Two faces split by role, with no third face anywhere
Separation by 1px hairline, the rail's left edge, and space, with no boxes and no shadows
Two real inks mixed in one cold hue family per scheme, with no grey and no opacity
One amber doing two jobs, every link and every live mark
Section labels in mono, uppercase and tracked, smaller than the body they introduce
Square corners everywhere, and marks drawn as 1px rules and 5px and 6px CSS squares
Tabular figures in the mono columns, proportional figures inside sentences
Browser chrome themed from the same palette: selection, scrollbar, focus ring

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Each scheme holds exactly two inks and one ground. The secondary ink is a mixed value in the same cold hue family as the primary, so no text colour is ever produced with opacity, a color-mix against grey, or a neutral grey hex. Audit test: grep the stylesheet for opacity and for any text colour outside the nine declared tokens; both return nothing.

rules.name: The One Amber, Two Jobs Rule
rules.body: The amber carries links and it marks what is live. Those are its only two jobs. A heading in amber, an amber fill behind a block, an amber border, or an amber figure inside a sentence each add a third job and are out.

rules.name: The No Ground Rule
rules.body: No element carries a background colour. The exceptions are the page ground itself, the opaque running head painted in that same ground, the CSS-drawn marks (the 6px live squares, the 5px bullet square, the 1px jump rule and the scrollbar thumb), and the skip link while it has focus. Separation everywhere else is a hairline and space.

rules.name: The Dark-First Rule
rules.body: The dark values are the declarations on :root and the light values are the override inside prefers-color-scheme: light. A new token is authored dark first and given its light counterpart in the same commit, so the two sets never drift apart.

rules.name: The Two Faces Rule
rules.body: Source Serif 4 sets everything a person wrote. Geist Mono sets everything a machine measured, plus the labels a reader scans: status, years and dates, latencies, sizes, counts, versions, stack names, proof links and section labels. Neither face does the other's job, so the mono never sets a sentence and never appears as a costume for "technical".

rules.name: The Inverted Label Rule
rules.body: A section label is smaller than the body it introduces, 12.5px mono against 17px and 18px serif. The label is the section's own name standing over a list of differently-named records, and it is set in diluted ink with a hairline under it so it reads as a tab on a register rather than as a headline.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: A mono line never sits above a heading. The heading comes first in source order inside every record and the rail is grid-placed into the first column beside it, so the single-column fold at 680px puts the name before the date without a reordering rule.

rules.name: The Figure-in-Sentence Rule
rules.body: A measured figure inside a sentence stays in the serif at weight 600 and takes the sentence's own proportional lining figures. Tabular lining figures belong to the mono columns, where digits have to line up under each other. Audit test: every tabular-nums declaration sits on a mono selector.

rules.name: The Two Left Edges Rule
rules.body: The page has exactly two left edges: the rail's, shared by the date rails and the section labels, and the prose's, shared by every sentence, heading, bullet and mono row in the stream. A block that sits outside a record grid, such as the opening sentence or the contact paragraph, is pushed to the prose edge with calc(var(--rail) + var(--rail-gap)). Centre nothing, ever.

rules.name: The Scan Column Rule
rules.body: A field a reader scans down the page rather than reads belongs in mono and belongs in the rail, aligned with the same field in the rows above and below it.

rules.name: The Heading-First Rule
rules.body: The heading is the first child of every record and the rail is grid-placed beside it. Source order is the reading order, so the single-column fold needs no order property and no second markup path.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Depth has exactly two values, rule and rule-soft, both at 1px. Use the stronger one where a rule opens a block, and the soft one between peers. A third weight, a shadow or a tinted panel is a new material and is out.

rules.name: The Opaque Bar Rule
rules.body: Nothing pinned to the viewport may blur or tint what scrolls under it. The running head is painted in the page ground at full opacity, and the pinned identity column carries no ground of its own.

rules.name: The Square Rule
rules.body: Content corners are square. A radius belongs only to browser chrome or to a focus ring that has to sit tight against a glyph.

dos: Do keep the two-column shell at 75.5rem with a 26px gutter, the identity column at clamp(15rem, 21vw, 19rem) and the stream at minmax(0, 1fr).
Do build every row as a rail grid, clamp(4.75rem, 6vw, 7rem) against minmax(0, 1fr) with a 28px gap, and put the heading first in source order.
Do push any block that sits outside a record grid onto the prose left edge with calc(var(--rail) + var(--rail-gap)).
Do author the dark values on :root and give every new token its light counterpart inside prefers-color-scheme: light in the same change.
Do carry separation with a 1px hairline (rule where a rule opens a block, rule-soft between peers) and with space.
Do split the two faces by role: Source Serif 4 for anything a person wrote, Geist Mono for anything a machine measured and for the labels a reader scans.
Do set a section label in mono at 12.5px tracked 0.1em and uppercased, in diluted ink, smaller than the body it introduces.
Do set a measured figure inside a sentence in the serif at 600 with proportional lining figures, and reserve tabular lining figures for the rail and the footer.
Do hold a plain paragraph at 68ch, a record's prose at 40rem, the italic gloss at 38rem, and the role line at 34ch.
Do write status as a mono word with a 6px filled amber square beside it, the same mark and the same size in a record's rail and beside the availability line.
Do spend the amber on links and on live marks, and on nothing else.
Do give :hover and :focus-visible identical treatment on the jump list, and reserve a transform for a slot whose length is already occupied, so no word on the page moves.
Do draw every mark in CSS or inline SVG, and theme the browser's own surfaces (selection, scrollbar, caret, focus ring, underline offset) from the same palette.
Do keep the page complete with no JavaScript, with motion disabled, under forced colours, and on paper.
donts: Don't put a background colour on any element. The page ground, the opaque running head, the CSS marks, the scrollbar thumb and the focused skip link are the whole list.
Don't box a record. No card, no panel, no border on four sides, no padding box, no radius on content.
Don't add a box-shadow, a filter, a backdrop-filter or a tinted layer anywhere, and never blur what scrolls under the running head.
Don't give the amber a third job. A heading, a fill, a border or a figure in amber is out.
Don't introduce a third face, and never set prose in the mono or a scanned label in the serif.
Don't bold the mono. The self-hosted file is one weight and there is no second cut to switch to.
Don't put a mono line above a heading, and don't reorder a record so the rail comes first in the source.
Don't set a section label larger than or equal to the body beneath it.
Don't stack a figure above its label as a metric tile, and don't round a measured number into a headline.
Don't derive a text colour with opacity or a neutral grey. Mix a new ink in the same cold hue family or use one of the two that exist.
Don't use a pill, a chip, a badge or a tag for status, a stack name or a year.
Don't animate a property that moves a word. The jump rule scales inside a slot it already fills, and the link underline changes colour, thickness and offset within its own line box.
Don't use a gradient, glass, a blurred blob, an emoji as an icon, a glyph icon font, or an indigo-to-violet accent. This page was rebuilt four times to get out of that vocabulary.
Don't add a costume. A volvelle, a pixel grid, an illuminated border and a sideways book were each built and rejected; the look is earned from type, measure and real data.
Don't ship a raster image. Decoration is CSS and inline SVG only.
Don't centre anything, and don't open with a hero carrying two buttons.
Don't let the pinned column stay sticky on a short window; it goes static under max-height: 700px so it cannot clip itself.
Don't let any text drop below WCAG AA on either ground; the current floor is the diluted ink at 5.1:1 on the light ground.
